_source: Ministry of Education / Curriculum Development Centre, Zambia. 'History Syllabus, Grade 10-12' (2013, published by CDC) — Grade 11, Part II: World History from 1870 to the Present, Topics 11.1-11.7. This is what is commonly referred to as 'World History' in the Zambian secondary syllabus: the unification of Germany, the Ottoman Empire, Britain, Russia, France, China, Japan and the USA to 1914, the European Alliance systems, the European Scramble for and Partition of Africa, the First World War, the inter-war era (Treaty of Versailles, Hitler, Mussolini, the Russian Revolution, the Spanish Civil War, China and Japan 1919-1939), the Second World War, post-1919 international peace organisations (League of Nations, UN, NATO, Non-Aligned Movement, Warsaw Pact), other international/regional organisations (Commonwealth, EU, OAU/AU, OAS, ECOWAS, Maghreb Union, Arab League, ASEAN, COMESA, SADC), and contemporary global issues. Topic, sub-topic and Specific Outcome statements only; the 'Content' column is omitted for the reasons documented in the Grade 10 file. This document's printed outcome numbering drifts badly throughout this Part (grade and topic digits leak into each other, e.g. codes printed as '14.4.1' or '12.4.1' for what is really Topic 11.4), so every outcome was reconstructed positionally against its sub-topic heading in the table's own reading order rather than trusting the printed codes. Under 11.7 (Contemporary Issues), the source names 11 sub-topics but only prints outcomes for 7 groupings — the first five sub-topics (Middle East Crises, DR Congo Regional Conflict, Rwanda Genocide, the Land Issue in Zimbabwe, International Terrorism) share two common outcomes about causes/consequences and conflict resolution rather than each having its own, so they are merged into one combined sub-topic entry here to avoid inventing per-topic outcomes not in the source. No topic on Korea exists anywhere in this real syllabus document (confirmed by a full read-through) — it is not included, since only real CDC content is used in this app; a summary chart at the end of the syllabus also names 'France, 1918-1939' and 'America, 1918-1939' as themes but no corresponding outcome text exists for them in the instructional table body, so they are likewise not included. The syllabus organizes content by Grade only, not by Term, so all of Grade 11 is modeled as a single term here.
